Subject: Qualification: storage scope & access controls — next steps

Hi Anika — great to meet earlier. Short recap + asks so we can qualify for the procurement/security track.

Call recap (high level):
- Use case: Clearsight will send clinical-like prompts (de-identified + some PHI identifiers in edge cases) to an endpoint for clinical summarization and patient messaging.
- Volume: pilot ~100K tokens/day; production forecast ~1.2M tokens/day.
- Primary concerns: what exactly Redwood persists for prompts/outputs, where (region), TTL options, and audit/logging controls for compliance.

Please confirm the following items (we've flagged what we need to move to legal/procurement):
1) What is stored by default when using Redwood hosted API — prompt input, generated output, and any intermediate caches (KV cache/chat history)?
2) For each stored artifact above, please state default retention, whether TTL is configurable per-customer or per-route, and if retention can be set to 0 (ephemeral).
3) Residency: Which AWS regions are used for storage of persisted artifacts, and can Clearsight require US-only storage for both active data and backups/snapshots?
4) Logging & audit: what logs (request metadata, token-level logs, full prompt text) are retained; retention periods for audit logs; options to export logs to customer S3/CloudWatch; and SOC2 evidence for logging processes.
5) Key management: default key model (Redwood-managed) vs. customer-managed KMS/HSM in Dedicated/Private.
6) Deletion APIs & SLA: is there a programmatic delete endpoint for prompt/output artifacts and what is the expected time-to-delete?
7) Data access controls: RBAC for internal Redwood engineers, documented break-glass workflows, and how redaction requests are handled.

Attachments: redwood-dataflow-diagram.png (diagram of typical hosted flow) and sca_requirements.xlsx (we noted Clearsight asked for a simple answers table).

Next steps: if you can confirm items 1–6 above or point me to your security contact, we can schedule a technical follow-up (SSO + KMS review) next week.

Thanks — Jonas

- Do you keep a copy of generated outputs? Our compliance team treats outputs that may include PHI the same as inputs.

Hi Anika — thanks for the questions, answered inline below. I've attached a brief CSV (answers-table.csv) with the same items for your questionnaire.

> Is prompt input stored by default in hosted mode? If so, for how long and is that configurable per-API key/route?
Short answer: For Redwood hosted API, prompt inputs and generated outputs may be persisted by default for debugging/quality for up to 30 days. Retention is configurable at the customer level for enterprise accounts — we can set per-route retention policies (e.g., 0 / 7 / 30 / 90 days). For Dedicated/Private deployments, customers can choose zero retention (ephemeral) for prompts and outputs.

> Do you keep a copy of generated outputs? Our compliance team treats outputs that may include PHI the same as inputs.
Yes — generated outputs are treated equivalently to inputs in our retention model. Defaults match the input retention above. We recommend setting TTL=0 for any route that may contain PHI unless you require auditability for a window.

> For debugging, do you keep token-level logs or full request bodies?
We capture request metadata (timestamps, model, route, token count) by default. Full request/response bodies are captured only when the customer enables "tracing/debug" for a route or if a support ticket requires trace capture; those captures are limited and timeboxed. Token-level logs are available as an opt-in for debugging; we can disable token-level capture for Clearsight.

> We require US-only storage for both data at rest and for backups/snapshots. Can you commit to that for a production environment?
Yes — hosted environment can be scoped to US regions only via account-level controls; backups and snapshots for those accounts are stored in US-only regions. For stricter isolation we recommend Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in a US region) or Private (customer-managed VPC) which provide stronger residency guarantees.

> Key control: we prefer customer-managed KMS in production. Is that available with Dedicated or Private only?
Correct: customer-managed KMS/HSM is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted accounts use Redwood-managed keys by default, but enterprise customers with specific requirements can work with our security team and account engineering to arrange a dedicated keying arrangement or deploy Private.

> Deletion SLA: we need a documented delete API and confirmation that deletions are honored across backups within 48 hours.
We provide a programmatic delete endpoint for persisted prompt/output artifacts. For Hosted accounts, deletion is usually reflected in primary storage within 24 hours and backup/snapshot propagation within 48–72 hours depending on snapshot cadence; we can commit to a 48-hour window for enterprise contracts (documented in the DPA/SLA). Dedicated/Private deployments have configurable snapshot cadence to meet stricter windows.

Notes on access controls and audit logs:
- Encryption: AES-256 for data at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- RBAC: role-based access controls with minimum-privilege for support engineers; access to request/response captures requires an approved support ticket and is logged.
- Audit logs: request metadata and admin actions kept for 365 days by default for enterprise; logs can be exported to customer S3, CloudWatch, or SIEM via streaming.

Attached: answers-table.csv (short answers matching your questionnaire). I've also linked our data-handling doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDocLink
